entities.name: Leprosy
entities.description: A chronic granulomatous infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium leprae and Mycobacterium lepromatosis, displaying exclusive tropism for Schwann cells and dermal histiocytes, causing anesthetic cutaneous lesions, peripheral nerve trunk enlargement, and progressive physical deformities.

entities.name: Tuberculoid Leprosy
entities.description: High-resistance polar form presenting with solitary or few well-demarcated hypopigmented or erythematous anesthetic plaques.

entities.name: Borderline Tuberculoid Leprosy
entities.description: Borderline spectrum form with multiple asymmetrical anesthetic plaques and satellite lesions.

entities.name: Mid-Borderline Leprosy
entities.description: Dimorphous intermediate form with inverted-saucer or swiss-cheese annular plaques.

entities.name: Borderline Lepromatous Leprosy
entities.description: Multibacillary form with numerous poorly defined plaques and partial sensory preservation.

entities.name: Lepromatous Leprosy
entities.description: Anergic polar form with widespread symmetric infiltration, macules, and lepromas.

entities.name: Indeterminate Leprosy
entities.description: Earliest transient stage presenting with faint hypopigmented macules and slight sensory loss.

entities.name: Pure Neural Leprosy
entities.description: Primary neural involvement without skin lesions, causing mononeuropathy multiplex.

entities.name: Histoid Leprosy
entities.description: Lepromatous variant presenting with succulent keloid-like nodules on normal skin.

entities.name: Lucio Leprosy
entities.description: Diffuse non-nodular lepromatous form with generalized shiny waxy dermal infiltration.

entities.name: Lucio Phenomenon
entities.description: Severe necrotizing vasculopathy with jagged purpura and cutaneous infarcts.

entities.name: Type 1 Reversal Reaction
entities.description: Delayed-type hypersensitivity reaction causing acute plaque erythema and neuritis.

entities.name: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum
entities.description: Type 2 immune-complex vasculitis with crops of tender subcutaneous nodules and fever.

entities.name: Silent Neuritis
entities.description: Asymptomatic progressive loss of nerve function without spontaneous pain or tenderness.

entities.name: Acute Leprous Neuritis
entities.description: Acute inflammatory nerve trunk swelling with intense pain, tenderness, and weakness.

entities.name: Chronic Neuropathic Pain
entities.description: Persistent dysesthesias and burning pain along fibrosed peripheral nerves.

entities.name: Atrophic Rhinitis
entities.description: Chronic nasal crusting, foul discharge, and mucosal atrophy from bacillary invasion.

entities.name: Nasal Septal Perforation
entities.description: Destruction and perforation of the cartilaginous nasal septum from subperichondrial infiltration.

entities.name: Leprous Orchitis
entities.description: Inflammatory testicular swelling and parenchyma destruction in multibacillary disease.

entities.name: Testicular Atrophy
entities.description: Bilateral fibrotic shrinkage of testes leading to hypogonadism, impotence, and sterility.

entities.name: Gynecomastia
entities.description: Endocrine-mediated glandular breast enlargement in males secondary to testicular failure.

entities.name: Chronic Iridocyclitis
entities.description: Granulomatous anterior uveitis causing iris pearls, synechiae, and visual loss.

entities.name: Exposure Keratitis
entities.description: Corneal drying, ulceration, and opacity resulting from paralytic lagophthalmos.

entities.name: Episcleritis
entities.description: Inflammatory congestion of episcleral tissue occurring during systemic ENL attacks.

entities.name: Corneal Hypesthesia
entities.description: Loss of protective corneal touch sensation from trigeminal nerve damage.

entities.name: Immune Complex Glomerulonephritis
entities.description: Renal glomerular injury driven by circulating immune complex deposition in ENL.

entities.name: Secondary Amyloidosis
entities.description: Systemic AA amyloid deposition in kidneys, liver, and spleen from chronic inflammation.

entities.name: Hepatic Granulomas
entities.description: Granulomatous histiocytic infiltration of Kupffer cells and liver parenchyma.

entities.name: Splenomegaly
entities.description: Enlargement of spleen from bacillary seeding and reticuloendothelial hyperplasia.

entities.name: Bone Marrow Bacillemia
entities.description: Marrow infiltration by bacilli-laden Virchow cells during bacteremic dissemination.

entities.name: Superficial Lymphadenopathy
entities.description: Rubbery, non-tender enlargement of lymph node chains draining affected skin.

entities.name: Dermal Anhidrosis
entities.description: Local cessation of eccrine sweat production caused by sympathetic denervation.

entities.name: Cutaneous Alopecia
entities.description: Destruction of hair follicles and alopecia within cutaneous leprous lesions.

entities.name: Acral Lymphedema
entities.description: Chronic non-pitting lymphedema of hands and feet from lymphatic obliteration.

entities.name: Ichthyosiform Skin Changes
entities.description: Dry, cracked, fish-scale skin xerosis from autonomic denervation and sebaceous atrophy.

entities.name: Plantar Neuropathic Ulceration
entities.description: Chronic painless mal perforant ulcers over weight-bearing points of the foot.

entities.name: Digital Acro-Osteolysis
entities.description: Painless trophic bone resorption and shortening of phalanges in fingers and toes.

entities.name: Leprous Dactylitis
entities.description: Fusiform inflammatory swelling of digits during acute Type 2 reactional states.

entities.name: Systemic Reactive Arthritis
entities.description: Polyarticular synovial inflammation and joint effusion occurring during ENL.

entities.name: Upper Airway Stridor
entities.description: Inspiratory stridor from mucosal infiltration and edema of laryngeal structures.

entities.name: Peripheral Autonomic Dysautonomia
entities.description: Microvascular dysregulation causing cyanosis, cold extremities, and vasomotor failure.

entities.name: Anesthetic Skin Patch
entities.description: Well-demarcated hypopigmented or erythematous patch with definite sensory loss.

entities.name: Ulnar Nerve Enlargement
entities.description: Palpably thickened, firm, tender nerve trunk proximal to the medial epicondyle.

entities.name: Common Peroneal Nerve Enlargement
entities.description: Palpable nerve trunk winding around the fibular neck, leading to foot drop.

entities.name: Great Auricular Nerve Enlargement
entities.description: Prominent visible and palpable nerve trunk crossing the sternocleidomastoid muscle.

entities.name: Posterior Tibial Nerve Thickening
entities.description: Palpable enlargement behind the medial malleolus causing plantar anesthesia.

entities.name: Radial Cutaneous Nerve Thickening
entities.description: Palpable superficial sensory nerve thickening over the distal radius.

entities.name: Median Nerve Thickening
entities.description: Palpable nerve swelling in the distal forearm above the flexor retinaculum.

entities.name: Facies Leontina
entities.description: Deep furrowing and nodular facial infiltration producing a lion-like appearance.

entities.name: Madarosis
entities.description: Bilateral loss of eyebrows and eyelashes commencing at the lateral margins.

entities.name: Claw Hand Deformity
entities.description: Intrinsic muscle paralysis causing hyperextension of MCP and flexion of IP joints.

entities.name: Lagophthalmos
entities.description: Inability to fully close palpebral fissures from orbicularis oculi paralysis.

entities.name: Foot Drop
entities.description: Paralytic loss of ankle dorsiflexion producing high-steppage compensatory gait.

entities.name: Saddle Nose Deformity
entities.description: Collapse of the cartilaginous nasal bridge following septal destruction.

entities.name: Pendulous Infiltrated Earlobes
entities.description: Thickened, elongated, nodular earlobes from histiocytic bacillary accumulation.

entities.name: Ape Hand Deformity
entities.description: Flattening of thenar eminence and loss of thumb opposition from median neuropathy.

entities.name: Wrist Drop Deformity
entities.description: Inability to extend wrist and fingers caused by radial motor nerve destruction.

entities.name: Hypothenar Muscle Atrophy
entities.description: Wasting and hollowing of hypothenar eminence resulting from ulnar denervation.

entities.name: First Web Space Wasting
entities.description: Deep guttering of dorsal interosseous muscle between thumb and index finger.

entities.name: Claw Toe Deformity
entities.description: Hyperextension of MTP and flexion of IP toe joints from intrinsic foot denervation.

entities.name: Mal Perforant Plantar Ulcer
entities.description: Indolent calloused trophic ulceration beneath metatarsal heads or heel.

entities.name: Corneal Opacification
entities.description: Scarring and haziness of cornea secondary to lagophthalmos and trauma.

entities.name: Iris Pearls
entities.description: Glistening tiny white granulomatous nodules along the pupillary margin.

entities.name: Ectropion
entities.description: Outward sagging and eversion of lower eyelid from facial nerve denervation.

entities.name: Tender Subcutaneous Nodules
entities.description: Eruption of painful erythematous subcutaneous nodules across limbs in ENL.

entities.name: Foveal Annular Plaques
entities.description: Plaques with punched-out hypochromic center and sloping borders in BB leprosy.

entities.name: Satellite Skin Lesions
entities.description: Smaller secondary anesthetic macules surrounding a dominant primary plaque.

entities.name: Cigarette Paper Wrinkling
entities.description: Fine atrophic wrinkling of epidermis over healing anesthetic tuberculoid plaques.

entities.name: Waddell High-Steppage Gait
entities.description: Exaggerated hip flexion gait pattern to lift a flaccid dropped foot.

entities.name: Slit-Skin Smear Acid-Fast Bacilli
entities.description: Identification of acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco stained dermal smears.

entities.name: Bacteriological Index Score
entities.description: Logarithmic quantification (0 to 6+) of bacillary density across dermal smears.

entities.name: Intracellular Dermal Globi
entities.description: Cigar-bundle clusters and dense aggregates of M. leprae inside Virchow cells.

entities.name: Morphological Index Determination
entities.description: Percentage of solid viable bacilli relative to fragmented non-viable forms.

entities.name: High-Resolution Nerve Ultrasound
entities.description: Bedside sonography showing nerve enlargement and loss of fascicular pattern.

entities.name: Nerve Cross-Sectional Area Enlargement
entities.description: Ultrasound cross-sectional area >10-12 mm² in ulnar or peroneal nerve trunks.

entities.name: Intraneural Hypervascular Doppler Flow
entities.description: Increased color Doppler endoneurial blood flow reflecting active neuritis.

entities.name: Hierarchical Cutaneous Sensory Loss
entities.description: Sequential loss of temperature first, light touch second, and pinprick pain last.

entities.name: Thermal Sensation Loss
entities.description: Failure to discriminate hot from cold water tubes applied to skin patches.

entities.name: Light Touch Monofilament Impairment
entities.description: Inability to perceive Semmes-Weinstein monofilaments on lesion testing.

entities.name: Pinprick Pain Hypoesthesia
entities.description: Diminished or absent perception of sharp pinprick sensation within lesions.

entities.name: Voluntary Muscle Testing Deficit
entities.description: Standardized MRC motor grading reduction in hand and foot intrinsic muscles.

entities.name: Lepromin Skin Test Negativity
entities.description: Absence of Mitsuda induration at 28 days indicating lepromatous anergy.

entities.name: Lepromin Skin Test Positivity
entities.description: Induration >5 mm at 28 days demonstrating intact cell-mediated immunity.

entities.name: Tuberculoid Dermal Epithelioid Granulomas
entities.description: Epithelioid granulomas with Langhans cells destroying cutaneous nerves.

entities.name: Lepromatous Foamy Virchow Histiocytes
entities.description: Diffuse sheets of lipid-laden foamy histiocytes packed with acid-fast bacilli.

entities.name: Grenz Zone Preservation
entities.description: Clear subepidermal band of uninvolved collagen above lepromatous infiltrate.

entities.name: Nerve Fascicle Fibrosis
entities.description: Endoneurial collagen deposition and axonal loss visualized on nerve biopsy.

entities.name: Anti-PGL-1 IgM Seropositivity
entities.description: Elevated serum IgM antibodies targeting M. leprae phenolic glycolipid-1.

entities.name: ML-Flow Lateral Flow Positivity
entities.description: Point-of-care lateral flow visual band detecting anti-PGL-1 IgM antibodies.

entities.name: Mycobacterium leprae PCR Positivity
entities.description: PCR amplification of specific RLEP repetitive element DNA sequences.

entities.name: Marked Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: Leukocytosis (15,000–25,000/µL) with left shift during Type 2 ENL episodes.

entities.name: Elevated Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate
entities.description: Marked ESR elevation (>80–120 mm/h) during acute inflammatory reactional states.

entities.name: Markedly Elevated C-Reactive Protein
entities.description: High serum CRP (>50–150 mg/L) marking systemic vasculitis in ENL attacks.

entities.name: Immune Complex Proteinuria
entities.description: Proteinuria resulting from immune-complex glomerulonephritis during ENL.

entities.name: Microscopic Hematuria
entities.description: Urinary red blood cell casts indicating active glomerular inflammation in ENL.

entities.name: Secondary Normocytic Normochromic Anemia
entities.description: Anemia of chronic disease and marrow reticuloendothelial iron blockade.

entities.name: Polyclonal Hypergammaglobulinemia
entities.description: Broad-based increase in gamma globulins with reversed A:G ratio in MB cases.

entities.name: Biologic False-Positive VDRL
entities.description: Positive non-treponemal syphilis serology with negative treponemal tests.

entities.name: Serum Tumor Necrosis Factor-Alpha
entities.description: High circulating TNF-alpha driving fever and tissue necrosis in ENL.

entities.name: Serum Interleukin-6 Elevation
entities.description: Elevated IL-6 reflecting B-cell activation and immune complex vasculitis.

entities.name: Decreased Serum Testosterone
entities.description: Subnormal testosterone levels from lepromatous destruction of Leydig cells.

entities.name: Elevated Luteinizing Hormone
entities.description: Compensatory rise in LH and FSH indicating primary testicular failure.

entities.name: Plain Radiography Acro-Osteolysis
entities.description: Pencil-pointing and cortical absorption of distal phalanges on X-ray.

entities.name: Soft Tissue Neuropathic Resorption
entities.description: Loss of terminal phalangeal soft tissue tufts from repeated microtrauma.

entities.name: Nerve Conduction Velocity Slowing
entities.description: Electromyographic motor and sensory slowing across enlarged nerve trunks.

entities.name: Reduced Sensory Action Potentials
entities.description: Severely attenuated or absent SNAP amplitudes documenting axonal loss.

entities.name: Intraneural Caseous Necrosis
entities.description: Fluid-filled cold nerve abscess cavities visualized on nerve sonography.

entities.name: Untreated Multibacillary Household Contact
entities.description: Cohabitation with an untreated patient discharging viable bacilli in droplets.

entities.name: Nasal Droplet Aerosol Transmission
entities.description: Inhalation of infectious droplets and dried secretions from coughing and sneezing.

entities.name: Nine-Banded Armadillo Exposure
entities.description: Contact with wild Dasypus novemcinctus, sylvatic reservoirs in the Americas.

entities.name: Red Squirrel Zoonotic Reservoir
entities.description: Sylvatic contact with wild Sciurus vulgaris harboring M. leprae in the UK.

entities.name: Non-Human Primate Reservoir
entities.description: Zoonotic contact with infected chimpanzees or sooty mangabeys in Africa.

entities.name: Superficial Skin Inoculation
entities.description: Percutaneous bacillary entry via preexisting skin cuts or microtrauma.

entities.name: Endemic Developing Country Residence
entities.description: Extended living or travel in tropical nations with ongoing endemic transmission.

entities.name: South-East Asia Regional Endemicity
entities.description: Residence in South-East Asia accounting for >70% of new global cases.

entities.name: Poverty and Household Crowding
entities.description: Crowded substandard living conditions facilitating droplet transmission.

entities.name: Pediatric Household Contact
entities.description: Children under 15 cohabiting with cases, marking active transmission.

entities.name: Multi-Year Incubation Period
entities.description: Paucibacillary disease incubation typically spanning 3 to 5 years.

entities.name: Decade-Long Incubation Period
entities.description: Multibacillary incubation extending 5 to 10 years, up to 20 years.

entities.name: Host Genetic Susceptibility
entities.description: Inherited polymorphisms altering macrophage handling of mycobacteria.

entities.name: HLA-DR2 and HLA-DR3 Alleles
entities.description: Class II HLA alleles conferring strong predisposition to tuberculoid disease.

entities.name: HLA-DQ1 Allele
entities.description: Class II HLA allele predisposing to anergic lepromatous leprosy forms.

entities.name: PARK2 and PACRG Polymorphisms
entities.description: Promoter variants impairing ubiquitin-mediated macrophage destruction of bacilli.

entities.name: MRC1 Exon 7 Polymorphisms
entities.description: Mannose receptor variants conferring vulnerability to multibacillary disease.

entities.name: Innate Natural Resistance
entities.description: Natural genetic immunity present in >95% of human population.

entities.name: Post-Exposure Household Prophylaxis
entities.description: Lack of single-dose rifampicin post-exposure prophylaxis increasing attack rate.

entities.name: Pregnancy and Puerperium
entities.description: Gestational immune shifts precipitating initial disease or reactional flares.

entities.name: Immunosuppressive Therapy Host
entities.description: Anti-TNF biologics and corticosteroids precipitating disease reactivation.

entities.name: Subclinical Upper Airway Carriage
entities.description: Transient nasal carriage and shedding in asymptomatic household contacts.

entities.name: Intact Cutaneous Temperature Sensation
entities.description: Completely preserved cold and warm sensation within a solitary skin lesion.

entities.name: Intact Fine Light Touch
entities.description: Normal light touch perception via nylon monofilaments inside skin patch.

entities.name: Severe Cutaneous Pruritus
entities.description: Intense itching, scratching, or excoriations within cutaneous lesions.

entities.name: Acute Symptom Onset
entities.description: Rapid onset of skin eruptions or nerve weakness over days to weeks.

entities.name: Normal Peripheral Nerve Caliber
entities.description: Absence of nerve enlargement or tenderness across all peripheral trunks.

entities.name: Preserved Sweating and Hair
entities.description: Intact sweating and hair follicle growth within an isolated macule.

entities.name: Strictly Symmetrical Polyneuropathy
entities.description: Length-dependent stocking-glove neuropathy lacking macules or nerve swelling.

entities.name: Rapid Ceftriaxone Clinical Response
entities.description: Rapid lesion clearance on cephalosporins or penicillins excludes M. leprae.

entities.name: Excoriated Pruritic Web Burrows
entities.description: Interdigital excoriated burrows with nocturnal itching from scabies mites.

entities.name: Central Spontaneous Ulcerative Slough
entities.description: Rapid necrotic ulceration and sloughing over days typical of pyoderma.

entities.name: Transient Migratory Skin Rash
entities.description: Evanescent wheals or plaques spontaneously resolving within 24–48 hours.

entities.name: Normal Slit-Skin Smears
entities.description: Repeatedly negative slit smears at cold sites rules out LL and BL disease.

entities.name: Prominent Mucosal Oral Aphthae
entities.description: Recurrent painful oral aphthous ulcerations typical of Behçet disease.

entities.name: Preserved Corneal Sensation
entities.description: Normal corneal touch reflexes in isolated peripheral facial palsy.

entities.name: Absence of Nerve Thickening
entities.description: Lack of palpable thickening across ulnar, peroneal, and auricular nerves.

entities.name: Rapid Defervescence on Penicillin
entities.description: Resolution of fever and tender nodules within 48 hours of penicillin.

entities.name: Epidermal Hyphae on KOH
entities.description: Fungal hyphae and spores on potassium hydroxide scraping examination.

entities.name: Normal Nerve Fascicular Architecture
entities.description: Preserved fascicular architecture and normal cross-sectional areas on US.

entities.name: Prominent Targetoid Lesions
entities.description: Concentric targetoid lesions with mucosal crusting in erythema multiforme.

entities.name: Acute Asymmetric Flaccid Paralysis
entities.description: Sudden painless lower motor neuron paralysis over 24–48 hours.

entities.name: Completely Intact Tendon Reflexes
entities.description: Brisk tendon reflexes with normal sensory exam in a limb rules out leprosy.

entities.name: Vitiligo
entities.description: Autoimmune depigmentation disorder with chalk-white macules and intact sensation.

entities.name: Pityriasis Versicolor
entities.description: Superficial fungal infection causing scaly macules with intact sensory function.

entities.name: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Protozoal ulcerations with indurated borders, intact sensation, and amastigotes.

entities.name: Sarcoidosis
entities.description: Systemic granulomatosis with non-caseating plaques, intact sensation, and adenopathy.

entities.name: Cutaneous Tuberculosis
entities.description: Lupus vulgaris plaques with apple-jelly nodules on diascopy and intact sensation.

entities.name: Diabetic Neuropathy
entities.description: Symmetric length-dependent polyneuropathy with chronic hyperglycemia and no macules.

entities.name: Granuloma Annulare
entities.description: Non-scaly annular erythematous plaques with preserved light touch and sweating.

entities.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
entities.description: Autoimmune disease with photosensitive malar rash, positive ANA, and intact sensation.

entities.name: Secondary Syphilis
entities.description: Papulosquamous rash on palms and soles with reactive treponemal tests and intact sensation.

entities.name: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
entities.description: Neurocutaneous disorder with café-au-lait spots and soft dermal neurofibromas.

entities.name: Pityriasis Alba
entities.description: Hypopigmented scaly facial patches in atopic individuals with normal sensation.

entities.name: Erythema Nodosum
entities.description: Tender pretibial subcutaneous nodules restricted to lower limbs with no bacilli.

entities.name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease
entities.description: Hereditary motor-sensory neuropathy with symmetric wasting, pes cavus, and family history.

entities.name: Post-Inflammatory Hypopigmentation
entities.description: Secondary pigmentary loss following dermatitis with normal cutaneous sensation.

entities.name: Mycosis Fungoides
entities.description: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with pruritic plaques, atypical lymphocytes, and normal nerves.

entities.name: Vasculitic Mononeuritis Multiplex
entities.description: Systemic vasculitis with multi-nerve palsies, positive ANCA, and no skin anesthesia.

entities.name: Amyloid Neuropathy
entities.description: Infiltrative neuropathy with autonomic failure and cardiomyopathy lacking macules.

entities.name: Diffuse Cutaneous Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Lepromatoid nodules teeming with Leishmania amastigotes with preserved sensation.

relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Presents at the high-resistance polar end with solitary or few (1–3) sharply demarcated, hypopigmented or erythematous scaly plaques showing prominent elevated outer margins, central clearing, complete anesthesia, alopecia, and anhidrosis.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Manifests with 4 to 10 asymmetrical, well-demarcated anesthetic plaques often surrounded by smaller characteristic satellite macules, accompanied by irregular and prominent thickening of adjacent peripheral nerves.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Presents with dimorphous annular erythematous plaques featuring characteristic punched-out hypochromic central areas and sloping, fading outer borders yielding a pathognomonic swiss-cheese or inverted-saucer morphology.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Presents with numerous, poorly defined, bilateral erythematous macules, papules, and infiltrated plaques distributed across the torso and limbs with variable or partial sensory impairment.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Represents the anergic multibacillary polar form with widespread, symmetrical, shiny hypochromic macules, diffuse dermal infiltration, and innumerable erythematous or copper-colored dermal nodules (lepromas).

[MANIFESTS_AS] Represents the earliest transient clinical stage presenting with one or few ill-defined hypopigmented flat macules with faint sensory diminution, preserved sweating, and no detectable nerve trunk thickening.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Presents as primary neurological involvement in the total absence of cutaneous skin lesions, characterized by mononeuritis or mononeuritis multiplex with pain, sensory loss, and palpable peripheral nerve enlargement.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Variant of lepromatous leprosy presenting with firm, circumscribed, succulent, keloid-like or fibroma-like cutaneous nodules and plaques arising over normal-appearing skin, containing spindle-shaped histiocytes packed with bacilli.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Diffuse non-nodular lepromatous variant characterized by generalized, shiny, waxy dermal infiltration, complete absence of discrete nodules, generalized alopecia, and diffuse anhydrosis.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Severe necrotizing cutaneous vasculopathy arising in Lucio or lepromatous leprosy marked by painful, purpuric, jagged geometric cutaneous infarctions leading to extensive ulceration and secondary sepsis.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute delayed-type (Type IV) hypersensitivity reaction in borderline patients causing sudden erythema, swelling, and desquamation of pre-existing skin plaques combined with excruciating acute peripheral neuritis.

relationships.keywords: MANIFESTS_AS, type 2 reaction, immune complex vasculitis
relationships.description: [MANIFESTS_AS] Type 2 immune complex-mediated (Type III) hypersensitivity vasculitis in multibacillary patients causing recurrent crops of intensely painful erythematous subcutaneous nodules, high fever, and systemic organ inflammation.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Insidious, asymptomatic deterioration of motor and sensory peripheral nerve function in the absence of spontaneous nerve pain or tenderness, frequently causing unnoticed permanent neurological deficits.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute inflammatory swelling of peripheral nerve trunks within unyielding fibro-osseous canals, presenting with intense lancinating pain, severe localized tenderness, and rapid drop in sensorimotor capacity.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Long-standing persistent burning, tingling, or lancinating dysesthesias resulting from irreversible intraneural fibrosis, axonopathy, and central sensitization following leprous nerve destruction.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Bacillary infiltration and autonomic denervation of the nasal mucosa causing chronic crusting, foul-smelling nasal discharge, mucosal pallor, decreased vascularity, and progressive mucosal atrophy.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Extensive lepromatous infiltration of the subperichondrium of the cartilaginous nasal septum resulting in avascular ischemic necrosis, septal perforation, and structural collapse.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Hematogenous bacillary invasion and immune-complex deposition in the testes during lepromatous disease and ENL, causing acute painful testicular swelling followed by parenchymal fibrosis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Progressive bilateral testicular shrinkage and destruction of androgen-producing Leydig cells and seminiferous tubules, culminating in primary hypogonadism, impotence, and azoospermia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Symmetrical glandular breast enlargement in male lepromatous patients caused by endocrine dysfunction, altered estrogen-to-androgen ratios, and primary testicular failure.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Granulomatous anterior uveitis caused by direct M. leprae invasion of the ciliary body and iris, producing miliary iris pearls, posterior synechiae, secondary glaucoma, and blindness.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Severe corneal desiccation, epithelial erosion, and secondary bacterial keratitis resulting from the inability to close the eyelids due to zygomatic branch facial nerve palsy.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Acute sectoral or diffuse inflammation of the episcleral tissue occurring frequently during systemic Type 2 ENL episodes, producing intense ocular pain, photophobia, and ciliary injection.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Blunting or complete absence of the corneal protective blink reflex caused by leprous destruction of the ophthalmic division sensory fibers of the trigeminal cranial nerve.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Renal involvement arising during severe Type 2 reactional states driven by circulating bacillary antigen-antibody immune complexes depositing in glomerular basement membranes.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Systemic deposition of amyloid A fibrillar protein in kidneys, spleen, and liver secondary to prolonged, chronic suppurative ulcers and recurrent ENL inflammatory reactions.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Asymptomatic miliary granulomatous infiltration of liver parenchyma and Kupffer cells by M. leprae, characterized by histiocytic clusters containing acid-fast bacilli in lepromatous patients.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Non-tender enlargement of the spleen caused by extensive reticuloendothelial bacillary seeding, macrophage phagocytosis of mycobacterial debris, and secondary amyloidosis.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Infiltration of the hematopoietic marrow by bacilli-laden Virchow histiocytes during persistent multibacillary bacteremia, contributing to secondary normocytic anemia and leukopenia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Painless, discrete, rubbery enlargement of peripheral lymph nodes draining affected cutaneous territories, including epitrochlear, axillary, and inguinal lymph node chains.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Localized or regional loss of sweat secretion within skin lesions caused by postganglionic sympathetic autonomic fiber destruction supplying eccrine sweat glands.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Complete loss of vellus and terminal hair within cutaneous plaques and over limbs resulting from leprous denervation and destructive infiltration of pilosebaceous units.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Chronic brawny non-pitting swelling of hands, forearms, lower legs, and feet caused by lymphatic vessel obliteration, recurrent erysipelas, and dependent vasomotor paralysis.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Dry, scaly, polygonally cracked, ichthyosis-like xerotic skin changes especially over the pretibial surfaces and distal limbs due to extensive autonomic denervation and sebaceous gland atrophy.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Development of deep, chronic, painless plantar ulcers over high-pressure weight-bearing zones of the foot following posterior tibial nerve sensory loss and unperceived repetitive trauma.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Progressive, painless trophic absorption, shortening, and resorption of phalangeal bones of fingers and toes secondary to repeated microtrauma, secondary osteomyelitis, and autonomic ischemia.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Painful, spindle-shaped, inflammatory fusiform swelling of the fingers and toes caused by acute periosteal and soft-tissue inflammation during severe Type 2 reactional flares.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Symmetrical polyarthritis and tenosynovitis involving wrists, metacarpophalangeal joints, and ankles occurring as a major clinical component of Type 2 immune-complex reactions.
[MANIFESTS_AS] Life-threatening inspiratory stridor and dyspnea caused by extensive lepromatous infiltration and acute inflammatory edema of the epiglottis, arytenoids, and vocal cords.

[MANIFESTS_AS] Impairment of sympathetic microvascular regulation leading to cyanotic cold extremities, postural hypotension, loss of vascular tone, and abnormal peripheral circulation in advanced disease.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Solitary or multiple hypopigmented or erythematous skin lesions showing definitive, objective impairment or total absence of thermal, tactile, and pinprick sensation constitutes the primary cardinal WHO diagnostic hallmark.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, peripheral nerve enlargement, ulnar nerve
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Palpable, firm, cord-like or spindle-shaped thickening and exquisite tenderness of the ulnar nerve trunk directly above the medial epicondyle and olecranon groove.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Palpably thickened, enlarged, and rolled peripheral nerve trunk palpable as it winds around the neck of the fibula, predisposing to peroneal nerve palsy.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, cervical nerve, great auricular nerve
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Prominently visible and palpable thickened nerve trunk running diagonally across the sternocleidomastoid muscle in the lateral neck when the patient rotates the head.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, posterior tibial nerve, medial malleolus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Palpable cord-like enlargement and tenderness of the posterior tibial nerve trunk as it passes posterior and inferior to the medial malleolus at the ankle.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, superficial radial nerve, anatomical snuffbox
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Palpable, superficial tender thickening of the sensory branch of the radial nerve crossing the anatomical snuffbox over the distal radius.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Palpable firm swelling and enlargement of the median nerve trunk in the lower forearm just proximal to the flexor retinaculum of the wrist.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Advanced lepromatous hallmark characterized by deep furrowing, massive infiltration of forehead and cheeks, and nodular coarsening producing a distinctive lion-like facial appearance.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Symmetrical thinning and complete bilateral loss of eyebrows (beginning laterally) and eyelashes due to direct M. leprae destruction of facial hair follicles.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, main en griffe, ulnar claw hand
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Classic neuropathic hand deformity with hyperextension of the metacarpophalangeal joints and acute flexion of interphalangeal joints in the 4th and 5th digits from intrinsic muscle paralysis.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, facial nerve palsy, incomplete eyelid closure
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Inability to achieve complete voluntary closure of the palpebral fissure due to orbicularis oculi paralysis from zygomatic branch facial nerve destruction, exposing the cornea.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, common peroneal palsy, steppage gait
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Inability to dorsiflex the foot and toes due to common peroneal motor nerve palsy, causing a high-steppage gait with dragging of the toes during ambulation.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, nasal bridge collapse, saddle nose
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Depressed nasal bridge and collapse of the cartilaginous nose resulting from lepromatous osteochondritis, mucosal destruction, and septal cartilage absorption.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Elongated, thickened, boggy, and hanging lobules of the external ears caused by diffuse histiocytic infiltration and bacillary accumulation in cooler ear tissue.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Severe flattening of the thenar eminence with external rotation and inability to oppose or abduct the thumb due to chronic median motor nerve destruction.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, radial nerve palsy, wrist drop
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Inability to extend the wrist, thumb, and metacarpophalangeal joints caused by radial motor nerve paralysis, seen in advanced triple-nerve upper limb palsy.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, ulnar motor wasting, hypothenar atrophy
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Prominent hollow depression, flattening, and wasting of the intrinsic muscles of the hypothenar eminence resulting from ulnar nerve motor denervation.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, dorsal interosseous wasting, first web space
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Deep guttering and atrophy of the first dorsal interosseous muscle between the metacarpals of the thumb and index finger, pathognomonic of ulnar motor neuropathy.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, claw toes, intrinsic foot denervation
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Marked hyperextension of metatarsophalangeal joints and flexion of interphalangeal joints of the toes caused by denervation of intrinsic foot muscles by the posterior tibial nerve.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, mal perforant, plantar neuropathic ulcer
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Deep, round, calloused, and indolent trophic ulceration on the plantar aspect of the metatarsal heads or heel occurring in the setting of complete plantar anesthesia.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Progressive haziness, vascularization, and scarring of the cornea resulting from unprotected exposure keratitis, trichiasis, or chronic interstitial keratitis.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Tiny, discrete, glistening, white miliary granulomatous nodules lining the pupillary margin of the iris, pathognomonic of lepromatous intraocular bacillary spread.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Outward sagging and eversion of the lower eyelid caused by paralytic atony of the orbicularis oculi and cutaneous cicatrization, leading to constant epiphora.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, inflammatory nodules, erythema nodosum leprosum
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Eruption of multiple, evanescent, exquisitely painful erythematous subcutaneous lumps and plaques across the extensor limbs, face, and trunk in Type 2 reactions.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, inverted saucer plaque, foveal lesion
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Characteristically shaped annular plaques with a sharply defined punched-out hypochromic central zone and sloping erythematous outer margin diagnostic of mid-borderline leprosy.

[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Small, distinct, anesthetic macular or papular lesions clustered immediately adjacent to the margin of a larger dominant anesthetic plaque in borderline tuberculoid leprosy.
[HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Thin, atrophic, dry, non-sweating epidermal wrinkling resembling fine cigarette paper over the central healing area of resolving tuberculoid plaques.

relationships.keywords: HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK, high-steppage gait, peroneal palsy gait
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Exaggerated hip and knee flexion lifting the leg high off the ground during ambulation to prevent the dropped, flaccid foot from scraping the floor.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Microscopic demonstration of slender, rod-shaped acid-alcohol-resistant bacilli stained red with modified Ziehl-Neelsen or Fite-Faraco technique on dermal slit smears.

[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Logarithmic quantification scale (0 to 6+) measuring bacillary density across 4 to 6 cooler anatomical slit sites, with BI >= 1+ definitively classifying multibacillary disease.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Dense spherical aggregates and parallel cigarette-pack clusters of M. leprae bacilli densely packed inside foamy histiocytes on slit-skin smear or biopsy.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Percentage assessment of solid, uniformly stained viable bacilli relative to fragmented and granular non-viable forms, serving as an index of therapeutic response.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside sonography demonstrating marked, asymmetrical nerve trunk swelling, disruption of fascicular echo-architecture, and hypoechoic endoneurial thickening.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, nerve cross-sectional area, sonographic enlargement
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Sonographic cross-sectional area enlargement of the ulnar nerve exceeding 10–12 mm² at the elbow or peroneal nerve at the fibular neck, indicating leprous neuropathy.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Prominent endoneurial and perineurial color Doppler signals demonstrating active intraneural hyperemia, a hallmark of acute neuritis and Type 1 reactional flares.

[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Predictable chronological pattern of sensory modality degradation within cutaneous lesions: loss of temperature discrimination first, light touch second, and pinprick pain last.

[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside sensory testing failure to differentiate between hot and cold water tubes applied to the skin lesion, representing the earliest sensitive physical sign of leprous neuropathy.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Inability to perceive Semmes-Weinstein 2.0g or 0.05g calibrated monofilament bristles on cutaneous lesions or distal palmar and plantar innervation territories.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Blunted or absent perception of sharp pain upon sterile pinprick stimulation within the boundaries of hypopigmented or erythematous skin plaques.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, voluntary muscle testing, motor denervation
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Standardized MRC motor grading reduction in abductor pollicis brevis, first dorsal interosseous, or tibialis anterior muscles documenting peripheral motor denervation.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Absence of delayed-type granulomatous induration at 28 days following intradermal lepromin injection (negative Mitsuda reaction), demonstrating lepromatous T-cell anergy.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, positive Mitsuda reaction, tuberculoid immunity
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Strong delayed hypersensitivity induration (>5 mm at 28 days, positive Mitsuda reaction) demonstrating intact, protective cell-mediated immunity in tuberculoid disease.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, epithelioid granuloma, dermal nerve destruction
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Full-thickness skin biopsy showing compact, non-caseating epithelioid cell granulomas with Langhans giant cells tracking and destroying cutaneous neurovascular bundles.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Histopathology revealing diffuse dermal sheets of lipid-laden, multivacuolated foamy macrophages (Virchow cells) teeming with innumerable acid-fast bacilli.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Characteristic histological subepidermal clear zone of normal uninvaded collagen separating the flattened epidermis from the dense lepromatous histiocytic dermal infiltrate.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Severe endoneurial collagen deposition, perineurial lamellar thickening, and progressive destruction of Schwann cell architecture visualized on nerve biopsy.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated circulating serum IgM antibodies specifically directed against M. leprae phenolic glycolipid-1 antigen, strongly correlated with high bacteriological indices.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Rapid bedside point-of-care immunochromatographic visual band confirming high titers of anti-PGL-1 antibodies, triaging patients directly into the multibacillary category.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Molecular amplification of the highly repetitive RLEP genomic insertion sequence from skin biopsy, slit smear, or nasal swab confirming mycobacterial DNA presence.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Complete blood count showing marked leukocytosis (WBC 15,000–25,000/µL) with prominent left shift and toxic granulation during acute Type 2 ENL episodes.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, elevated ESR, acute phase reactants
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Marked elevation of the erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR >80–120 mm/h) reflecting intense systemic immune-complex inflammatory activity in ENL.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Sharp rise in serum C-reactive protein (CRP >50–150 mg/L) serving as an objective biochemical marker of systemic vasculitis and reactional severity.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Detection of significant urinary protein excretion (>1–3 g/24h) reflecting secondary immune-complex deposition glomerulonephritis during recurrent ENL attacks.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urinalysis demonstrating dysmorphic red blood cells and red cell casts indicating active glomerular inflammation in leprosy reactional states.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Hematological profile showing normocytic normochromic anemia of chronic disease and reticuloendothelial iron sequestration in advanced lepromatous patients.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Serum protein electrophoresis revealing a broad-based polyclonal increase in gamma globulins with an inverted albumin-to-globulin ratio in multibacillary disease.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Positive non-treponemal syphilis serology (VDRL or RPR) with negative specific treponemal tests (FTA-ABS) due to cross-reacting anti-phospholipid antibodies in LL.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Markedly elevated circulating serum levels of TNF-alpha correlating with systemic pro-inflammatory toxicity, fever, and tissue damage during ENL reactions.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, IL-6 elevation, immune complex vasculitis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Elevated circulating IL-6 concentrations reflecting robust Th2-mediated B-cell activation and systemic immune complex-driven vasculitis in Type 2 reactions.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, low testosterone, Leydig cell destruction
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Subnormal total and bioavailable serum testosterone levels resulting from primary destruction of testicular Leydig cells by lepromatous orchitis.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Compensatory pituitary hypersecretion of LH and FSH (hypergonadotropic hypogonadism) in response to primary lepromatous testicular gonadal failure.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Plain skeletal radiographs showing progressive tapering, cortical thinning, and pencil-pointing resorption of the distal phalanges and metatarsal heads.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, soft tissue resorption, digital shortening
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Radiographic demonstration of concentric concentric digital shortening and total loss of terminal phalangeal soft tissue tufts from repeated painless microtrauma.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Electromyography showing marked slowing of motor and sensory conduction velocities and prolonged distal latencies across thickened peripheral nerve segments.
[EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Absent or severely attenuated sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitudes in the ulnar, median, or sural nerves demonstrating axonal sensory loss.

relationships.keywords: EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN, cold nerve abscess, intraneural necrosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Identification of focal hypoechoic, fluid-filled cold nerve abscess cavities and caseous necrosis within the peripheral nerve trunk on neuromuscular sonography.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Prolonged, intimate cohabitation with an untreated index multibacillary leprosy patient who discharges millions of viable bacilli from the upper respiratory tract.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Respiratory inhalation of infectious droplets and dried nasal mucosal secretions expelled during coughing and sneezing by untreated multibacillary patients.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Direct zoonotic contact, hunting, butchering, skinning, or consumption of wild nine-banded armadillos (Dasypus novemcinctus), natural hosts of M. leprae in the Americas.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Sylvatic exposure to wild Eurasian red squirrels (Sciurus vulgaris) in the British Isles, which harbor endemic clinical M. leprae and M. lepromatosis infections.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Zoonotic contact with naturally infected non-human primates, including chimpanzees and sooty mangabeys, which serve as animal reservoirs of M. leprae in Africa.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Percutaneous entry of bacilli via preexisting cutaneous abrasions, skin trauma, or contaminated sharp instruments in close proximity to infected cases.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Long-term residence, migration, or extended travel in tropical and subtropical countries where sustained domestic transmission of M. leprae persists.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Residence in the WHO South-East Asia region, primarily India and Indonesia, which accounts for greater than 70% of all newly diagnosed leprosy cases globally.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Substandard socioeconomic living conditions and overcrowded, poorly ventilated domestic environments that maximize continuous respiratory droplet exposure.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Children under 15 years living in household contact with untreated patients, representing a high-risk cohort and sentinel indicator of active local transmission.
[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Paucibacillary leprosy exhibits an extraordinarily prolonged average incubation period of 3 to 5 years before the appearance of initial anesthetic macules.
[INCUBATION_PERIOD] Multibacillary leprosy exhibits an exceptionally long incubation latency spanning 5 to 10 years, and occasionally extending up to 20 years before diagnosis.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Inherited host susceptibility driven by genomic variations in PRKN, PACRG, MRC1, NOD2, RIPK2, and LRRK2 genes controlling innate macrophage defenses.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Individuals expressing human leukocyte antigen class II alleles HLA-DR2 and HLA-DR3 possess significant immunological predisposition toward tuberculoid leprosy.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Individuals expressing the human leukocyte antigen class II allele HLA-DQ1 exhibit pronounced genetic susceptibility to anergic lepromatous leprosy.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Single-nucleotide polymorphisms in the co-regulated PARK2 and PACRG promoter region impair macrophage ubiquitin-proteasome responses to M. leprae infection.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Genetic polymorphisms in exon 7 of the MRC1 gene encoding the macrophage mannose receptor increase host vulnerability to multibacillary disease.

relationships.keywords: HIGH_RISK_HOST, natural resistance, low attack rate
relationships.description: [HIGH_RISK_HOST] Over 95% of human populations possess innate genetic immunity and cell-mediated resistance, remaining completely healthy and asymptomatic upon exposure.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Omission of single-dose rifampicin post-exposure prophylaxis (SDR-PEP) among documented household and close social contacts increases subsequent clinical attack rates.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Gestational immunomodulation and rapid postpartum cell-mediated rebound frequently unmask latent leprosy or precipitate severe Type 1 and Type 2 reactional flares.
[HIGH_RISK_HOST] Patients receiving systemic anti-TNF biologic agents, immunosuppressants, or prolonged corticosteroid regimens can experience accelerated reactivation of latent infection.
[EXPOSURE_TO] Asymptomatic household contacts harboring M. leprae DNA in nasal swabs act as transient subclinical carriers and community reservoirs for disease transmission.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, preserved temperature sensation, exclusion boundary
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Finding completely normal and preserved thermal discrimination (cold vs. warm) within a solitary skin lesion definitively rules out tuberculoid and borderline leprosy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal light touch, preserved sensation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal, preserved light touch sensation using Semmes-Weinstein monofilaments across all boundaries of an isolated cutaneous patch rules out leprosy plaques.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Presence of intense itching, scratching, or excoriated dermatitis within skin lesions rules out typical leprosy patches, which are non-pruritic and anesthetic.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid explosive onset and progression of cutaneous lesions or peripheral neuropathy over days to weeks firmly rules out the indolent multi-year course of leprosy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal nerve caliber, absence of hypertrophy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of peripheral nerve trunk thickening, tenderness, or cross-sectional enlargement on exam and ultrasound rules out primary pure neural leprosy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, preserved sweating, intact hair follicles
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Normal eccrine sweating response and intact follicular hair growth inside an isolated hypopigmented macule rules out denervating tuberculoid leprosy.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Strictly symmetrical, length-dependent distal stocking-glove sensory polyneuropathy without cutaneous anesthetic macules or palpable nerve trunks rules out leprosy.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid clinical healing and clearance of skin lesions in response to standard beta-lactams or third-generation cephalosporins firmly rules out M. leprae infection.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, scabies burrows, excoriated web spaces
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Identification of intensely itchy serpiginous web-space burrows with nocturnal exacerbation characteristic of Sarcoptes scabiei infestation rules out leprosy.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Acute spontaneous purulent breakdown and rapidly progressing central ulceration over several days rules out slowly evolving granulomatous leprosy lesions.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Evanescent or migratory erythematous wheals and plaques that spontaneously resolve within 24 to 48 hours without scarring rule out chronic leprous lesions.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, negative slit smears, lepromatous exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Repeatedly negative slit-skin smears at multiple cool peripheral sites (earlobes, elbows, active margins) firmly rules out lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Recurrent, painful, self-limiting oral aphthous ulcerations typical of Behçet syndrome or Crohn disease rules out standard oral leprosy involvement.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, preserved corneal reflex, Bell palsy
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Fully preserved, normal bilateral corneal touch reflexes in an isolated peripheral facial palsy rules out trigeminal nerve involvement of leprosy.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, absent nerve hypertrophy, non-leprous mononeuritis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Absolute lack of palpable nerve trunk thickening in the ulnar, common peroneal, posterior tibial, and great auricular nerves rules out leprous mononeuritis multiplex.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Rapid defervescence and resolution of tender inflammatory cutaneous nodules within 24–48 hours of penicillin therapy excludes Type 2 ENL reactions.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Microscopic detection of branching fungal hyphae or budding yeast clusters on skin scraping potassium hydroxide (KOH) examination rules out leprosy patches.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, normal nerve sonography, intact fascicles
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] High-resolution neuromuscular ultrasound demonstrating preserved endoneurial fascicular architecture and normal cross-sectional areas rules out active leprous neuritis.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, target lesions, erythema multiforme major
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Acute self-limited concentric three-zone targetoid skin lesions with mucosal involvement characteristic of erythema multiforme major rules out leprosy reactions.

relationships.keywords: RULED_OUT_BY, acute flaccid paralysis, anterior horn disease
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Sudden painless flaccid limb paralysis developing over 24 to 48 hours without preceding sensory impairment rules out chronic leprous mononeuritis.
[RULED_OUT_BY] Normal, brisk deep tendon reflexes combined with preserved light touch and pinprick sensation in an extremity rules out advanced leprous sensorimotor neuropathy.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Completely depigmented chalk-white macules in vitiligo retain intact thermal and light touch sensation, normal hair follicles, preserved sweating, and lack enlarged nerves.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Superficial fine-scaling hypopigmented patches in pityriasis versicolor feature intact sensation, normal peripheral nerves, and characteristic fungal hyphae on KOH prep.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Volcano-like indurated ulcerations in cutaneous leishmaniasis maintain fully intact local tactile sensation, spare peripheral nerve trunks, and show Leishmania amastigotes on smear.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Sarcoid granulomatous dermal plaques feature intact cutaneous sensation, normal nerve trunks, elevated serum ACE, and bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy on chest imaging.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Lupus vulgaris plaques display apple-jelly nodules on diascopy with completely preserved tactile sensation, no peripheral nerve involvement, and positive tuberculin skin test.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Diabetic peripheral polyneuropathy is strictly symmetrical and length-dependent, correlates with chronic hyperglycemia, and lacks cutaneous anesthetic macules or focal nerve thickening.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Non-scaly annular dermal plaques of granuloma annulare maintain completely preserved light touch and pinprick sensation, normal eccrine sweating, and normal peripheral nerves.

relationships.keywords: DIFFERENTIATED_FROM, look-alike, autoimmune connective tissue disease
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Malar photosensitive rash in systemic lupus erythematosus maintains intact sensation, normal peripheral nerve caliber, positive anti-dsDNA/ANA antibodies, and multisystem flares.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Papulosquamous copper-colored rash in secondary syphilis involves palms and soles with intact cutaneous sensation, generalized adenopathy, and reactive treponemal serology.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Neurofibromatosis presents with soft, compressible, painless dermal neurofibromas and café-au-lait macules without loss of thermal sensation or bacillary infiltration.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Ill-defined hypopigmented dry facial patches in young atopic patients preserve intact thermal and fine tactile sensation, normal sweating, and normal peripheral nerves.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Idiopathic erythema nodosum produces tender pretibial nodules restricted to lower legs, resolving without ulceration over 3–6 weeks, and lacks slit-skin acid-fast bacilli.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Hereditary motor-sensory neuropathy produces symmetric distal wasting, pes cavus, and hammer toes with strong family history, lacking anesthetic skin macules.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Hypopigmented macules following prior burns or dermatitis retain completely normal thermal and light touch perception, intact sweating, and unaffected nerve trunks.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma plaques present with poikiloderma, intense intractable pruritus, atypical epidermotropic lymphocytes on biopsy, and normal nerve trunks.

[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Systemic vasculitides like polyarteritis nodosa produce acute painful multi-nerve palsies with systemic constitutional signs, positive ANCA, and normal skin sensation outside deficits.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Familial or AL amyloid neuropathy presents with autonomic failure and restrictive cardiomyopathy, lacking focal hypopigmented anesthetic skin macules or bacillary globi.
[DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Diffuse lepromatoid nodules in diffuse cutaneous leishmaniasis maintain preserved cutaneous tactile sensation, normal nerve trunks, and show Leishmania amastigotes on smear.
